[FACT] User is experimenting with different types of plants in their garden, including basil, mint, and parsley.  
[EVENT] User attended a gardening workshop in their neighborhood on the same day, where they learned about companion planting and crop rotation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Choosing the right fertilizer for herbs can make a big difference in their health and productivity.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For herbs like basil, mint, and parsley, focus on fertilizers that provide a balanced mix of nutrients.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended fertilizers include Miracle-Gro Shake 'n Feed All Purpose Plant Food (organic, slow-release), Espoma Organic Indoor! 8-2-4 Herb & Vegetable Fertilizer (organic, water-soluble), and Schultz Super Bloom! Plant Food (synthetic, water-soluble).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested to always follow the instructions on the fertilizer package and start with a small amount to avoid over-fertilizing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Companion planting can help deter pests and attract beneficial insects, while crop rotation can prevent soil depletion and reduce the risk of disease.  
[USER] User has been using compost as a fertilizer for their herbs.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Compost is an excellent choice as a fertilizer for herbs, being nutrient-rich and improving soil structure.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested methods to use compost include mixing it into the soil, using it as a top dressing, or making compost tea.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended to ensure compost is fully broken down before use and to avoid using too much compost.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested natural methods to control whiteflies include using yellow sticky traps, insecticidal soap, neem oil, predatory insects, and vacuuming.
